messages:
Maya: quick q — thinking about revisiting per-org rate policy. instead of single RPM/TPM + flat concurrency, what if we used a stepped windows model to give predictable short bursts but enforce longer-term fairness?

Alex: stepped windows? like multiple token buckets layered by window length? e.g. 1s concurrency, 60s RPM, 1h TPM?

Maya: yeah. the goal: allow short-lived high qps (chat typing spikes) without letting a noisy tenant burn all hourly budget. also want smoothness for UI charts and easier console explainability. :thinking:

Sam: +1 on the problem. current flat RPM makes quick interactive workflows either throttle or need huge burst credits. curious about implementation complexity: how do we enforce multi-window efficiently at the router?

Nikhil: implementation sketch: evaluate windows in descending order, charge tokens in each relevant bucket. avoid per-request cross-network calls by keeping a local leaky-bucket cache with async reconciliation to central store. fallback to best-effort if store unreachable.

Jess: can we avoid racey double-charges? maybe a neat trick: maintain primary bucket atomicity on the token allocation path (fast path), and use eventual counters for analytics only. if primary fails, deny-fast to preserve fairness.

Maya: here's a config prototype for the console (not final):

```
rate_policy:
  kind: stepped
  windows:
    - name: instant
      window_sec: 1
      concurrency: 12
    - name: minute
      window_sec: 60
      rpm: 600
    - name: hour
      window_sec: 3600
      tpm: 5000
  burst_credits: 120
  refill_strategy: proportional
```

Alex: that looks readable. UI-wise we can show a stacked bar: instant vs minute vs hour capacity and current usage. also provide "explain why I was throttled" link that shows which window triggered.

Sam: Ops question — how do we migrate existing tenants? we have customers tuned to current RPM. rolling default to stepped might break them.

Maya: proposal: opt-in flag + telemetry for a month, then gradual default switch for new orgs only. provide "compatibility mode" that maps existing RPM to a stepped profile (automated shim).

Nikhil: for enforcement, hot path should be O(1) memops per-request. suggestion: per-router in-memory counters keyed by org with a small LRU and periodic flush, plus centralized enforcement for very large orgs. avoids network hop for common cases.

Jess: what about burst credits accounting? we need a graceful refill and UX in console to purchase or set policies. also how to map to billing (are bursts billable immediately or amortized?).

Maya: billing idea: charge tokens at use time; if bursts exceed baseline, show predicted monthly delta. let finance flag certain orgs as "post-pay" so we don't auto-block them.

Sam: telemetry signals to add: per-window rejection rate, median wait time (for queued concurrency), burst credit balance over time, and cause breakdown (instant/minute/hour). we should add these to per-tenant telemetry + alerting defaults.

Alex: edge-case: long-lived streaming connections holding concurrency slot for >60s. do we treat streaming separately (streaming-concurrency pool) to avoid eating minute RPM?

Maya: agree — recommend separate slot accounting for streaming vs completion calls. streaming slots consumed differently (charged per-second or per-message). need policy docs.

infra-bot: Deploy preview created: preview/rate-policy/stepped-1998765455. Config schema validated. Note: migration flags default to off.

Nikhil: next steps I can take: prototype router fast-path counters, simulate 3 workload shapes (burst, sustained, chat-typing) and show fairness + cost delta. anyone want to co-own the evaluation?

Jess: happy to help on console UX and billing mapping. can sketch mockups and edge-case flows.

Alex: I'll add a short RFC draft with the config schema, fallback semantics, and migration plan. target for draft in 1 week.

Maya: awesome. thanks all. leaving notes in the doc: https://redwood.internal/ratepolicies/stepped-proposal (draft). :thumbsup:
